ko.description:
**공자 · 논어 · I.16**

앞면은 아래 인용 원문을 직접 번역한 문장입니다. 해설·질문·관계는 편집 내용입니다.

### 맥락

공자는 남에게 인정받는 일보다 남을 이해하는 일을 자신의 과제로 삼는다.

### 오늘의 사례로 읽기 · 편집 해설

대화 중 다음에 할 멋진 답을 준비하느라 상대가 무엇을 걱정하는지 놓쳤다고 하자. 잠시 자신의 평가를 뒤로 두고 “가장 어려운 부분이 어디인가요?”라고 확인하면 대화의 목적이 달라질 수 있다. 이 편집 예시는 인정받을 필요를 부정하지 않고 주의의 방향을 옮기는 방법을 보여 준다. 상대를 이해하려는 질문도 답하고 싶지 않은 범위까지 캐묻는 권리는 아니다.

경청의 출발점을 평가받기에서 알아가기 쪽으로 옮겨 볼 수 있다.

### 나에게 묻기

최근 내가 이해하려 하기보다 인정받으려 했던 대화는 무엇인가?

### 주의할 점

타인의 인정이 생계나 안전에 영향을 미치는 현실까지 무시하라는 뜻은 아니다.

### 인용 원문

> I will not be afflicted at men's not knowing me; I will be afflicted that I do not know men.

[Analects](https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/3330/pg3330-images.html) · I.16

James Legge translation, The Chinese Classics; Project Gutenberg \#3330

en-US.description:
**Confucius · Analects · I.16**

The front preserves the quotation from the cited edition. Commentary, questions and connections are editorial.

### Context

Confucius redirects concern from being recognized to understanding other people.

### A present-day example · editorial commentary

Preparing an impressive reply can make it easy to miss what the other person is worried about. Asking which part is hardest may redirect attention from how you appear to what needs understanding. This editorial example does not deny a legitimate need for recognition; it changes the immediate focus of a conversation. Interest in another person also does not create a right to question them beyond what they wish to share. Listening includes respecting that boundary.

### A perspective

This invites us to enter a conversation as an inquirer rather than an applicant for approval.

### Reflect

In which recent conversation did I seek recognition more than understanding?

### Keep in mind

Recognition can materially affect safety and livelihood; this does not erase that fact.

### Source quotation

> I will not be afflicted at men's not knowing me; I will be afflicted that I do not know men.

### Source

[Analects](https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/3330/pg3330-images.html) · I.16

孔子は、人に認められることより人を理解することを自らの課題とする。

評価されることから知ろうとすることへ、聞く姿勢を移せる。

### 自分への問い

最近、理解するより認められようとした会話は何だったか。

### 注意点

他者の評価が生活や安全を左右する現実を無視する教えではない。

### 出典の原文

> I will not be afflicted at men's not knowing me; I will be afflicted that I do not know men.

### 맥락

공자는 사람을 평가하는 일과 말의 가치를 판단하는 일을 구별한다.

### 오늘의 사례로 읽기 · 편집 해설

좋아하지 않는 동료가 지적했더라도 보고서의 합계가 틀렸는지는 직접 계산해 확인할 수 있다. 그 지적이 맞는다는 사실이 그 사람의 모든 판단을 믿어야 한다는 뜻도 아니다. 이 편집 사례에서는 구체적인 주장의 근거와 사람 전체에 대한 평가를 나눈다. 직접 확인하기 어려운 전문적 주장이라면 발언자의 관련 지식과 이해관계도 근거를 평가하는 일부가 된다.

### 나에게 묻기

### 인용 원문

> The superior man does not promote a man simply on account of his words, nor does he put aside good words because of the man.

### 출처

The superior man does not promote a man simply on account of his words, nor does he put aside good words because of the man.
— Confucius
en-US.description:
**Confucius · Analects · XV.22 (Legge numbering)**

The front preserves the quotation from the cited edition. Commentary, questions and connections are editorial.

### Context

Confucius separates judging a speaker from judging the value of a statement.

### A present-day example · editorial commentary

A colleague you dislike can still point out an incorrect total that you can check directly. Accepting that correction does not require accepting every judgment the colleague makes. This editorial case separates evidence for a specific claim from an overall evaluation of the speaker. When a technical claim cannot readily be checked, relevant expertise and interests also matter. Separating person and claim is therefore a discipline of evaluation, not a demand to ignore the context of testimony.

### A perspective

A disliked speaker may still offer something worth examining.

### Reflect

What claim have I dismissed because of my feelings about its speaker?

### Keep in mind

Expertise and conflicts of interest remain relevant to assessing credibility.

### Source quotation

> The superior man does not promote a man simply on account of his words, nor does he put aside good words because of the man.

### Source

[Analects](https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/3330/pg3330-images.html) · XV.22 (Legge numbering)

James Legge translation, The Chinese Classics; Project Gutenberg \#3330

ja.title:
君子は言葉だけで人を登用せず、その人を理由に良い言葉を捨てない。
— 孔子
ja.description:
**孔子 · 論語 · XV.22 （レッグ訳の章節番号）**

表面は下記の引用原文からの独自訳です。解説・問い・関係は編集によるものです。

### 文脈

孔子は人物の評価と言葉の価値の判断を分ける。

### 今日の事例で読む・編集解説

苦手な同僚の指摘でも、合計が誤りかは直接計算して確かめられる。訂正を受け入れても、その人の全判断を信じる必要はない。この編集例は特定主張の根拠と人物全体の評価を分ける。直接確認しにくい専門的主張なら、関連知識や利害も重要になる。人と主張の区別は評価の方法であり、証言の背景を無視せよという要求ではない。

### 読みの視点

苦手な相手の発言にも検討すべき点があるかもしれない。

### 自分への問い

話し手への感情のために退けた主張は何か。

### 注意点

信頼性を判断する際、専門性や利害関係はなお重要である。

### 出典の原文

> The superior man does not promote a man simply on account of his words, nor does he put aside good words because of the man.

### 出典

[Analects](https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/3330/pg3330-images.html) · XV.22 (Legge numbering)

James Legge translation, The Chinese Classics; Project Gutenberg \#3330

— 孔子

**孔子 · 論語 · XV.22 （理雅各譯本章節編號）**

正面是根據下列引文所作的自譯。解說、提問與關聯由編輯撰寫。

### 脈絡

孔子區分對人的評價與對言論價值的判斷。

### 從今日案例閱讀・編輯解說

不喜歡的同事指出合計錯誤，仍可直接計算確認；接受這項更正，不表示須接受對方所有判斷。這個編輯案例分開特定主張的證據與對說話者的整體評價。若專業主張不易親自驗證，相關知識與利益關係也重要。因此區分人與話，是評估方法，不是忽略證言脈絡的要求。

### 閱讀觀點

不喜歡的人也可能提出值得考慮的觀點。

### 自我提問

我曾因對說話者的感受而忽略什麼主張？

### 注意事項

評估可信度時，專業能力與利益關係仍然重要。

### 出處原文

> The superior man does not promote a man simply on account of his words, nor does he put aside good words because of the man.

### 出處

And let him be sure to leave other men, their turns to speak.
— Francis Bacon
en-US.description:
**Francis Bacon · Essays · Of Discourse**

The front preserves the quotation from the cited edition. Commentary, questions and connections are editorial.

### Context

Bacon warns that questions can become an interrogation and asks speakers to share the floor.

### A present-day example · editorial commentary

Asking another question before the first is answered can interrupt the thinking that interest was meant to invite. Waiting after a question and checking whether anything remains to be said can make room. This editorial example examines the quality of a turn, not just its duration. Someone who finds immediate speech difficult may need a written channel too. Equal minutes alone do not ensure equal access to being heard or equal freedom to use them.

### A perspective

We can assess a conversation by the room we leave, not just the questions we ask.

### Reflect

Whose turn will I consciously protect in my next conversation?

### Keep in mind

Equal speaking time alone cannot resolve differences in power or accessibility.

### Source quotation

> And let him be sure to leave other men, their turns to speak.

### Source

[Essays](https://www.gutenberg.org/files/575/575-h/575-h.htm) · Of Discourse

English original (1625 collection); Project Gutenberg \#575
